outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Not listing an exhaustive spec sheet (camera, weight, dimensions, etc.) is a minor omission because the task only asked to “find technical specs,” not necessarily every category.

Critical issues: The agent’s delivered specs contain multiple unsupported/incorrect claims relative to the provided Apple Tech Specs semantic DOM evidence. Specifically, it states (1) “Wi‑Fi 7” (not present anywhere in the retrieved DOM snippets), (2) “up to 18 hours of battery life” (the evidence shows only a testing methodology footnote, not an explicit hour figure), (3) “16–32GB unified memory” which conflicts with the visible options block showing “24GB or 32GB unified memory” (16GB appears only as a testing configuration in a footnote, not as an option list), and (4) “13.6- or 15.3-inch” display sizes, which are not evidenced in the retrieved snippets (only “13-inch” and “15-inch” appear in a testing footnote plus a “Liquid Retina display” header).

What is supported: The agent did navigate to Apple’s official MacBook Air Tech Specs page (https://www.apple.com/macbook-air/specs/) and some specs it reported are supported by the DOM evidence: Apple M5 is clearly referenced; an option lists “M5 with 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU”; storage options include “1TB, 2TB, or 4TB SSD” (supporting ‘up to 4TB’); and the ports section includes “Two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports.”

Outcome assessment: Although the agent reached the correct Apple specs page, the final output (the primary deliverable) mixes several correct items with several key fabricated/incorrect items. Because the user asked for technical specs, accuracy is central; an average user would not be satisfied with a spec summary that includes multiple major ungrounded claims (wireless standard, battery life, memory range, exact display sizes). Therefore, the task is not successfully completed as delivered.
